Dubai Police Expands Exotic Cop Car Lineup With New Lamborghini Temerario
8 photos
Photo: Dubai Police
The Lamborghini Temerario has already established itself as being a great supercar from the modern era. In fact, it is so fantastic that it has become a police car.
The plug-in hybrid exotic model has officially joined Dubai’s police fleet. The local force recently announced that the Temerario has entered its portfolio, which comprises numerous high-end models, some of which are on the very rare side of things. The vehicle has been introduced in partnership with Lamborghini Abu Dhabi and Dubai, and it will take on the usual tourist policing duties and engagement with residents and visitors.
“ Our luxury patrol fleet represents an innovative approach to policing, combining an effective security presence with community and tourist engagement, ” said the Director of the General Department of Criminal Investigation at Dubai Police, Brigadier Saeed Al Hajri. “ These vehicles help people feel safe, showcase Dubai’s positive image to visitors from around the world, and raise awareness of police services and public safety. Above all, they reinforce our commitment to being a police force that is close to the community. ”
Dubai’s police dropped shared an image in the press release that reveals the Lamborghini Temerario dressed in the usual attire. It combines white and green in a distinctive pattern, and also features a pair of emergency lights at the top part of the front windscreen. We reckon additional modifications could be on deck to better help the plug-in hybrid supercar with its new role, though that’s our two cents, and should be taken with the proverbial pinch of salt.
Photo: Lamborghini It is worth reminding ourselves that the Dubai police fleet is constantly growing with all kinds of exotic models. Over the years, we have seen the Bugatti Veyron, Ferrari FF, Lamborghini Aventador, Porsche 918 Spyder, Brabus Mercedes G 63, Lotus Eletre, Mercedes- AMG GT 63 S, a few Mansory-tuned vehicles, including the Ferrari Purosangue and Lmborghini Revuelto, and others. And it looks like there is also a Tesla Cybertruck that wears the same livery.
Mind you, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) is not the only country to have such a cop car, because the Lamborghini Temerario has also joined Italy’s state police department. The announcement was made a little over a month ago, at the beginning of September, 2026, and that ride will be used for “ the most important services, ” according to the local authorities, which include “the emergency transport of organs and medical supplies.”
In this case, Italy’s Lamborghini Temerario cop car features a white and blue livery, and it is decorated with the Italian flag on certain elements. It also features an emergency light bar on the roof, and likely other elements that we are unaware of. And in both cases, there are no mechanical upgrades, because the supercars that have joined Italy’s and the UAE’s police fleets retain their stock firepower.
What does that mean? Well, no fewer than three electric motors assisting the twin-turbocharged V8 engine, which has a 4.0-liter displacement. The ICE alone pumps out 789 hp (800 ps/588 kW) between 9,000 and 9,750 rpm. In total, the supercar boasts 907 brake horsepower (920 ps/677 kW) and 538 pound-feet (730 Nm) of torque. It features an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission, all-wheel drive, and a lithium-ion battery pack.
Photo: Lamborghini Lamborghini’s Temerario takes a mere 2.7 seconds to hit 62 mph (100 kph) from a standstill, the model’s spec sheet reveals, and can keep pushing all the way up to 213 mph (343 kph). It also has a tiny electric range of a few miles for short driving in the zero-emission mode. For the 2027 model year, you are looking at just under $400,000 for a brand new example in the United States of America, and that makes it over $200,000 more affordable than its bigger, punchier, and faster sibling, the Revuelto.
The Lamborghini Temerario was unveiled during the 2024 Monterey Car Week, and it hit the assembly line the following year at the Sant’Agata Bolognese factory. The model replaced the Huracan in the Raging Bull’s exotic car lineup, and it is now the brand’s new “baby” supercar. The same underpinnings have been used for the Audi Nuvolari, which is limited to 499 units, and will hit production toward the end of this year, featuring a very quirky design.
So far, the Lamborghini Temerario family comprises a single member, the one that we have dedicated numerous stories to. However, a Spyder , which is Lambo slang for convertible, is being developed as we speak, and will rock the same hardware, though due to the added weight, it should be a tiny bit slower than its fixed-roof sibling.
The Lamborghini Temerario Spyder is expected to debut in late 2026 or early 2027, and further down the line, the company will keep expanding the lineup with all sort of different versions, which are expected to become faster and faster with each one. After all, its predecessor, the Huracan , came in various variants over the years.
